title: Growing Arrays with realloc
summary: realloc resizes a heap block, moving it if it has to. Assign its result to a temporary so a failure does not lose the old block. A growing array keeps a length and a capacity and doubles the capacity when it is full, so adding stays fast on average - the same trick as Python lists and C++ vectors.

cards.q: What can realloc do when the block cannot grow where it is?
cards.a:
Allocate a new block, copy the data and free the old one

That is why old pointers into the block become invalid.

cards.q: Why is p = realloc(p, n) a bug?
cards.a:
If realloc fails, the only pointer to the old block is lost

Use a temporary variable.

cards.q: Why does a growing array double its capacity instead of adding one?
cards.a:
So copying is rare and adding is fast on average

Doubling gives amortised constant-time adds; growing by one would copy everything on every add.

cards.q: What do length and capacity mean?
cards.a:
Elements in use, and elements there is room for

When length reaches capacity, grow.
